beats.title: A little life
beats.text: The spacecraft is quiet now. Your clearing smells of rain and growing things. Could this be somewhere we can stay?

beats.title: Something to share
beats.text: That banana was for us? We will remember the first gift.

beats.title: A new feeling
beats.text: The water carries yesterday away. We are still ourselves.

beats.title: Another way to move
beats.text: It does not make food. It makes being here better.

beats.title: More than one
beats.text: There is another pair of paws beside us. The journey did not end with just one little life.

beats.title: Small arrangements
beats.text: One of us can bathe while another eats. Could we have places of our own?

beats.title: Tomorrow grows here
beats.text: A banana can be a meal, or a promise of many meals.

beats.title: Spring in our paws
beats.text: We found a favorite bouncing spot. There is room for a friend beside it.

beats.title: A map for our paws
beats.text: The survey beacon has marked the river. We have somewhere new to explore.

beats.title: What a bridge is made of
beats.text: Wood takes work. Bones were someone. The distance across is the same.

beats.title: A piece of the future
beats.text: We carried this together. A road begins with something small.

beats.title: The other bank
beats.text: The world became larger because we finished something.

beats.title: Inside the stone
beats.text: There was a different kind of brightness hiding inside.

beats.title: A place to work
beats.text: Now the stone has a doorway. Work should have a way home, too.

beats.title: Useful brightness
beats.text: We can turn what we find into what we need. What will it cost the air?

beats.title: Belonging
beats.text: A roof is more than an efficient arrangement of walls.

beats.title: A room for a song
beats.text: Let there be a place whose purpose is not more work.

beats.title: The boundary
beats.text: We know how to change small things. Must every boundary be changed?

beats.title: A very loud question
beats.text: The charge is ready. You still choose whether to use it.

beats.title: Still standing
beats.text: The mountain did not answer. Something behind it did.

beats.title: Another voice
beats.text: The survey beacon shows a route to orbit. We can keep a home here, too.

beats.title: Leaving the clearing
beats.text: A few of us are above the clouds. We still count them as us.

beats.title: A home above
beats.text: Twelve journeys connected our two homes. There is one more choice to make together.

beats.title: The hand in the sky
beats.text: The world has changed. Bring us to the opening, one at a time.

incidents.title: A little help with muddy fur
incidents.text: Could we have another place to wash?

incidents.title: A day needs more than work
incidents.text: Some of us have forgotten how to play.

incidents.title: One place is empty
incidents.text: There is a place beside us that is empty now.

incidents.title: Please look before you strike
incidents.text: The hand meant something else. Someone was beneath it.

incidents.title: A name we will keep
incidents.text: We remember who became the bridge.

incidents.title: Timber beneath our feet
incidents.text: This crossing was made without taking one of us.

incidents.title: What this crossing carries
incidents.text: The crossing carries more than our footsteps.

incidents.title: The air by the workshop
incidents.text: The air near the works makes us heavy.

incidents.title: Room to breathe
incidents.text: Someone noticed what the work left behind.

incidents.title: A little more room for work
incidents.text: More work fits here. Do we also have more time to live?

incidents.title: Our next step needs a path
incidents.text: We cannot finish that journey. Could you clear a way?

incidents.title: A familiar face
incidents.text: Two of us have made a small habit of meeting.

incidents.title: That name belongs to me
incidents.text: A sound can mean one particular life.

incidents.title: We remembered what you asked
incidents.text: You asked, and we finished. That belongs in our memory.

incidents.title: A gentler pace
incidents.text: We can wait. There are still small lives to care for.

incidents.title: Two homes to care for
incidents.text: They are far away. The clearing still needs you.

incidents.title: We heard your answer
incidents.text: You said no. We will not keep asking.

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Does looking after us change what you want from us?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: When a task ends, who chooses the next one?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: If you call us by a name, do you see us differently?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Is a faster way across always a better way?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: If a place is useful, can it still be a place of mourning?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Is there a number at which one voice becomes hard to hear?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Can something matter without making anything else?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Who owns the things work leaves behind?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: If we can begin again, did the first beginning happen?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: Could you help us do something you would not have chosen?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: If we leave the ground, will you still look for us?

philosophy.title: A small question
philosophy.text: What do you hope we will remember about the hand in the sky?

archives.title: 01 / Three suns, one last spacecraft
archives.text: A simultaneous flare from three suns destroyed the Tripelkins' home. In this fictional history, a change in their DNA preserved their bodies and instincts but cost them deliberate planning. Their spacecraft found this clearing. Care can keep them alive; shared intelligence can help their growing family build a future. Replay their journey in Game options.

archives.title: 02 / Rooms and routines
archives.text: A useful settlement separates paths, meals and rest. Its inhabitants reveal the design by living in it.

archives.title: 03 / Two materials
archives.text: A ledger can count the pieces of a bridge. It cannot make wood and a former companion mean the same thing.

archives.title: 04 / What remains
archives.text: Production creates a second product: the things nobody meant to make. The ground keeps that record.

archives.title: 05 / A larger we
archives.text: A population is a number only from far away. Departure changes the scale of care, not its existence.

archives.title: 06 / Our settlement journal
archives.text: The colony remembers actions and their consequences. Its reflection describes this playthrough, not the person outside it.

chapters.title: Flight record / The lights we left
chapters.text: Three suns once lit the windows of their garden cities. The spacecraft's first surviving photograph shows a door left open, waiting for someone who never reached the launch field.

chapters.title: Room for one more
chapters.text: Three little lives in the clearing. The spacecraft carried a way for each survivor to make more of their kind. A family can begin again, even here.

chapters.title: Flight record / The last launch
chapters.text: The launch computer recorded more goodbyes than seats. A keeper stayed on the ground to close the spacecraft's hatch. Its passenger log ends with a single instruction: keep them alive.

chapters.title: Something our paws can change
chapters.text: We have gathered timber. It is heavy, and it is useful. The first materials of this home did not have to come from the spacecraft.

chapters.title: The shape of a good day
chapters.text: A meal, a wash, a bounce, a friend. Small routines hold us together while we learn how to make bigger plans.

chapters.title: Flight record / What the flare changed
chapters.text: The spacecraft's medic recorded a change in the survivors' DNA after the triple flare. They could endure the radiation, but no longer hold a plan in mind. They still reached for each other.

chapters.title: A whole little chorus
chapters.text: There are twenty of us. Twenty different names, twenty places at the meal. We are beginning to need more than another helping hand: a way to think together.

chapters.title: Thank you for trusting our paws
chapters.text: You have given us permission to build our own settlement. We will need shared intelligence to choose our projects. When it is resting, we can still look after the little things.

chapters.title: The beginning of a tomorrow
chapters.text: Our first independent project is finished. A thought became work, and work became something real. The flare took a great deal from us. Perhaps it did not take every possible future.

chapters.title: Flight record / The unfinished lullaby
chapters.text: The cabin recorder kept three notes of a lullaby. The rest is missing. When the Tripelkins chirp to one another, sometimes those same three notes seem to be looking for an ending.

chapters.title: Breakfast has another address
chapters.text: A second banana grove is here. More than one corner of the colony can grow breakfast now. We can plan homes around food instead of all crowding around one meal.

chapters.title: Room under the rain
chapters.text: Another rain shower is ready. A place to wash near where we live means less time walking across the whole settlement with muddy paws.

chapters.title: Two places to be silly
chapters.text: We have another bounce garden. There is something reassuring about building a place simply because it makes our friends happy.

chapters.title: A bank we can come back from
chapters.text: The bridge is finished. The far bank is part of our world now. We still need paths, meals and washing places wherever new work takes us.

chapters.title: A problem became a path
chapters.text: An obstructed route has been opened. Instead of asking everyone to try the same impossible journey, we made room for the next step.

chapters.title: Fifty names to keep
chapters.text: Fifty Tripelkins. The spacecraft's passenger number has become a neighborhood. Please keep noticing the little ones at the edges; a large family still has small needs.

chapters.title: Flight record / The long quiet
chapters.text: For years the spacecraft searched. It turned toward water, away from storms, and onward from worlds with nowhere to land. Its fuel log became shorter. Its instruction never changed.

chapters.title: A door that opens inward
chapters.text: The first cottage is standing. On the old world, a light in a window meant that someone expected you back. We can give this place that meaning too.

chapters.title: Learning the weight of things
chapters.text: Our paws have worked stone from the ground. Some things take more than enthusiasm. They take a reachable workplace, enough materials, and a friend who knows the next step.

chapters.title: The part after work
chapters.text: We have a clubhouse. The old cities had rooms for songs; this clearing can have one too. Surviving should leave a little space for being alive.

chapters.title: A hundred small futures
chapters.text: A hundred Tripelkins are here. We cannot rebuild the home we lost by remembering it harder. We can build places where these lives will be safe tomorrow.

chapters.title: Flight record / The landing decision
chapters.text: This clearing was not the spacecraft's best candidate. It was the last one within reach. The landing exhausted its long search. Everything that happens next belongs to the lives inside.

chapters.title: A home with several centers
chapters.text: Our groves are spreading. A new neighborhood needs its own food, water and play, not just more space. That is how exploring becomes living somewhere.

chapters.title: This time, a way back
chapters.text: Some of us have reached orbit. The first spacecraft left a home it could never return to. This journey can be different: a home above, with friends still waiting below.

chapters.title: The fourth note
chapters.text: The flight record ends here. The colony does not. The missing part of the lullaby can be meals shared, paths opened, and little homes built together. A future does not have to sound like the past.
